envelope.text: four policies are transcribed exactly, but nano-ros publishes no

why: the QoS `/rosout` log publication uses (transient-local, keep-last(1000), 10 s lifespan). We publish no `/rosout` at all: `nros_log` composes a `&'static [&dyn LogSink]` and the `/rosout` sink is listed there as future work (nros-log/src/lib.rs:17, and `nros-tests/tests/logging.rs` says the macros are deferred along with it), while `rclcpp::NodeOptions::enable_rosout` (`packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/options.hpp:256`) is a REFUSE-LOUD `static_assert` — it was an inert bool in the since-deleted `rclcpp_compat.hpp` until phase-417 W3. A user loses `ros2 topic echo /rosout` on a nano-ros node -- logs land on the board console. The node-option spelling of the same decision is `cpp:NodeOptions::rosout_qos`, already recorded in the node stage. COLLAPSE CHECK 2026-09-04 (phase-417): `rclcpp::RosoutQoS` now ships in `packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/qos.hpp:985` (in `rclcpp_compat.hpp` until phase-417 stage 6 step A deleted it) (phase-417 W3.f), with its four policies transcribed exactly, so this correlates `same` on the PORTED surface. THE BOUND RECORDED HERE IS ABOUT THE TOPIC: nano-ros publishes no `/rosout`, so the name is a profile you can apply to a topic of your own rather than one the runtime is already using -- ADOPT-BOUNDED on exactly that point. The row survives because `--check` gates the NATIVE bucket, where this is still `theirs-only`. FAMILY SETTLED (phase-467 Q4, 2026-09-25) -- THE `/rosout` FAMILY CONTRADICTED ITSELF AND THIS ROW HELD THE HALF THAT WAS WRONG. Four rows record one fact between them (`cpp:RosoutQoS`, `cpp:RosoutQoS::RosoutQoS`, `cpp:NodeOptions::rosout_qos`, `c:logging_rosout_enabled`), and they disagreed about what kind of fact it is: this row said the `/rosout` decline "IS ABOUT THE TOPIC AND IT STANDS", while `c:logging_rosout_enabled` recorded the identical absence as an open `gap`. Both cannot be true of one topic. SETTLED AS A GAP, for three reasons. (1) NOBODY DECIDED: the book says `/rosout` is "explicitly out of scope TODAY", the sink list was SHAPED for a `RosoutSink` alongside `PlatformSink`, `rcl_interfaces/msg/Log` already ships as a pre-generated crate, and the `add_sink` tee hook is documented as the place a bridge would attach -- that is a thing not yet built, not a thing refused. (2) THE TWO VERDICTS ARE ASYMMETRICALLY REVERSIBLE: a wrong `gap` costs one ledger edit when someone notices, while a wrong `declined` removes the item from the queue permanently and nothing ever re-asks. (3) `enable_rosout` refuses because there IS no `/rosout` topic, not because one is impossible -- a different sentence, and the refusal is per-CONCEPT on `cpp:NodeOptions`, not a judgement about the topic. WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE: the TYPE ships. `rclcpp::RosoutQoS` is on the ported surface with its four policies transcribed, so this row is not and never was an absence of the profile -- which is why the verdict moves to `divergence` rather than to `gap`. The gap is the TOPIC, and it is tracked at `c:logging_rosout_enabled`, the one row whose subject that is. CITES RE-MEASURED 2026-09-25 (phase-467 Q4): `qos.hpp:745` -> `:985` and `options.hpp:250` -> `:256`. Recorded because the correction list this pass started from said `:977` for the first of those -- itself already stale, measured before ~88 commits landed on `main`. A cite is only worth what the day it was taken is worth; re-measure rather than copy one forward.
